intro.text: This entry describes pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome 8 (PPGL8), one of a group of genetically distinct hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes. I cannot reliably recall which gene is assigned to this type, so no causal gene is given here.

checks.claim: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome 8 (PPGL8) is one of a group of genetically distinct hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract never mentions PPGL8 or a numbered series of syndromes. It describes new susceptibility loci on chromosome 2cen and 16p13 in one family.

paragraphs.text: Hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes are tumor-predisposition disorders. Affected people develop neuroendocrine tumors of the adrenal medulla (pheochromocytoma) or of extraadrenal sympathetic or parasympathetic paraganglia (paraganglioma). Tumors may be multiple, may produce catecholamines, and some become metastatic.

checks.claim: Hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes are tumor-predisposition disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: This finding provides evidence for two novel susceptibility loci for pheochromocytoma and adds a recessive digenic trait to the increasingly broad genetic heterogeneity of these tumors.
checks.explanation: The abstract talks about familial susceptibility and hereditary disorders but does not use the term 'tumor-predisposition disorders' for PPGL syndromes in general.

checks.claim: People with hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes develop neuroendocrine tumors of the adrenal medulla (pheochromocytoma).
checks.evidence_quote: Pheochromocytomas are catecholamine-secreting tumors that result from mutations of at least six different genes as components of distinct autosomal dominant disorders.
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms that people with these hereditary disorders get pheochromocytomas. It does not say the tumors arise in the adrenal medulla or call them neuroendocrine.

checks.claim: People with hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes develop neuroendocrine tumors of extraadrenal sympathetic or parasympathetic paraganglia (paraganglioma).
checks.evidence_quote: Extra-adrenal tumors occurred in 28 mutation carriers (48%) and in 23 of 29 SDHA mutation carriers (79%), particularly with head and neck paraganglioma.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions extra-adrenal tumors and head and neck paraganglioma but does not describe sympathetic or parasympathetic paraganglia, or neuroendocrine origin.

checks.claim: Tumors in hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes may be multiple.
checks.evidence_quote: Fifty-three of 58 patients (91%) had familial, multiple, extra-adrenal, and/or malignant tumors and/or were younger than 40 years.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that patients had multiple tumors.

checks.claim: Tumors in hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes may produce catecholamines.
checks.explanation: The abstract states directly that these tumors secrete catecholamines.

checks.claim: Some tumors in hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndromes become metastatic.
checks.evidence_quote: Newly uncovered are 7 of 63 (11%) malignant pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas in SDHA and TMEM127 disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports malignant tumors, which I treated as equivalent to metastatic.

paragraphs.text: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma is genetically heterogeneous. Susceptibility genes include the succinate dehydrogenase complex genes (SDHD, SDHAF2, SDHC, SDHB and SDHA), as well as TMEM127, MAX, VHL, RET, NF1, FH and other genes involved in the Krebs cycle and hypoxia signaling.

checks.evidence_quote: adds a recessive digenic trait to the increasingly broad genetic heterogeneity of these tumors
checks.explanation: The abstract explicitly describes genetic heterogeneity.

checks.claim: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility genes include the succinate dehydrogenase complex genes SDHD, SDHAF2, SDHC, SDHB and SDHA.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the SDHx genes (SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHAF2 coding for succinate dehydrogenase subunits A, B, C, D, assembly factor 2)
checks.explanation: The paper lists all five SDH-complex genes.

checks.claim: TMEM127 is a pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified the transmembrane-encoding gene TMEM127 on chromosome 2q11 as a new pheochromocytoma susceptibility gene.
checks.explanation: The paper directly identifies TMEM127 as a pheochromocytoma susceptibility gene.

checks.claim: MAX is a pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The expanding etiology for hereditary pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas has recently included SDHA, TMEM127, MAX, and SDHAF2 as susceptibility genes.
checks.explanation: The abstract names MAX as a susceptibility gene.

checks.claim: VHL is a pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility gene.
checks.evidence_quote: additional pheochromocytomas with mutations in other pheochromocytoma susceptibility genes (8 RET-, 4 NF1-, 8 VHL- and 15 SDHB- or SDHD-mutant tumors)
checks.explanation: VHL is listed among the pheochromocytoma susceptibility genes.

checks.claim: RET is a pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility gene.
checks.evidence_quote: additional pheochromocytomas with mutations in other pheochromocytoma susceptibility genes (8 RET-, 4 NF1-, 8 VHL- and 15 SDHB- or SDHD-mutant tumors)
checks.explanation: RET is listed among the pheochromocytoma susceptibility genes.

checks.claim: NF1 is a pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility gene.
checks.evidence_quote: additional pheochromocytomas with mutations in other pheochromocytoma susceptibility genes (8 RET-, 4 NF1-, 8 VHL- and 15 SDHB- or SDHD-mutant tumors)
checks.explanation: NF1 is listed among the pheochromocytoma susceptibility genes.

checks.claim: FH is a pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility gene.
checks.evidence_quote: with more rarely identified genes including MAX (MYC-associated factor X), FH (fumarate hydratase) and TMEM127 (transmembrane protein 127)
checks.explanation: FH is listed as a susceptibility gene.

checks.claim: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma susceptibility genes include other genes involved in the Krebs cycle and hypoxia signaling.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not mention the Krebs cycle or hypoxia signaling.
